name: add_blocked_by
title: Add Blocked By Tool
description:
Mark native GitHub "blocked by" dependencies on an issue. 'issue_number' is the
blocked issue; 'blocked_by' is an array of issue numbers in the same repo that
block it. Declare the acting 'agent' — the links are set by that agent's GitHub
App through GitHub's native issue dependency graph (not a comment). Additive and
idempotent: links that already exist are skipped, none are ever removed. Requires
index.mcp.write scope.

agent.description:
The agent identity performing this action: 'holmes', 'watson', or 'lestrade'.
Declare your own name — the action is signed by that agent's GitHub App.

blocked_by.description: Issue numbers in the same repo that block 'issue_number'.

name: add_comment
title: Add Comment Tool
description:
Post a comment on a project item's GitHub Issue, or on a specific PR conversation when
'pr_number' is given (use this for Holmes's review notes and Watson's block questions,
which live on the PR). Declare the acting 'agent' — the comment is posted by that
agent's GitHub App. Body is markdown. Requires index.mcp.write scope.

agent.description:
The agent identity performing this action: 'holmes', 'watson', or 'lestrade'.
Declare your own name — the action is signed by that agent's GitHub App.

id.description: project_items.id of the item to comment on.

pr_number.description: Optional: comment on this PR's conversation instead of the issue.

name: check_repo_access
title: Check Repo Access Tool
description:
Report whether The Index's GitHub App governs a repository — i.e. whether
agent work for that repo should be dispatched through this MCP (signed by an
agent's GitHub App) or fall back to the plain gh CLI. Authenticates as the
App (App JWT) and checks GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/installation: 200 means
governed, 404 means not. Rate limits and 5xx surface as errors, never as a
false 'governed: false'. Results cache for ~5 minutes per repo.

name: claim_item
title: Claim Item Tool
description:
Mark a project item as being actively worked, so 'list_development_items' stops
offering it to a second agent. Dr. Watson calls this when it takes an item, and
'release_item' on every exit path. Refuses when the item is already claimed —
a live claim means another run owns it, and a stale one means the previous run
died and Dispatch should release it before re-dispatching. Requires the
index.mcp.write scope.

id.description: The project_items.id to claim (NOT the GitHub issue number).

name: close_as_duplicate
title: Close As Duplicate Tool
description:
Close issues as duplicates of a canonical issue via GitHub's native
duplicate relationship. 'canonical' is the surviving issue; 'duplicates'
is an array of issue numbers in the same repo to close as duplicates of
it. Declare the acting 'agent' — each duplicate is closed (state reason
DUPLICATE) and linked to the canonical by that agent's GitHub App, not a
comment. Idempotent: an issue already closed as a duplicate of the same
canonical is skipped, and an issue cannot be a duplicate of itself.
Requires index.mcp.write scope.

agent.description:
The agent identity performing this action: 'holmes', 'watson', or 'lestrade'.
Declare your own name — the action is signed by that agent's GitHub App.

canonical.description: The surviving issue's number — duplicates are linked to it and closed in its favor.

duplicates.description: Issue numbers in the same repo to close as duplicates of 'canonical'.

name: create_issue
title: Create Issue Tool
description:
Open a new GitHub issue as the acting agent and land it in the dev-team
pipeline in one call: the issue is created by that agent's GitHub App
(declare 'agent'), added to the configured project board, and — on org
repos — stamped with a native issue Type ('PBI' by default; pass 'type'
to override). Use this for Holmes's non-blocking review follow-ups and
any agent-authored issue, instead of a raw `gh issue create` the server
never sees. Board-add and Type are best-effort and reported under
'board'/'issue.type'; they never fail the create, and on user-owned repos
the Type is silently skipped. Requires index.mcp.write scope.

agent.description:
The agent identity performing this action: 'holmes', 'watson', or 'lestrade'.
Declare your own name — the action is signed by that agent's GitHub App.

type.description:
Optional native issue Type name (e.g. 'PBI', 'Product Goal'). Omit to
auto-stamp 'PBI' on org repos. Resolved case-insensitively against the
owner's issue-type catalog; silently skipped on user-owned repos.

name: find_item
title: Find Item Tool
description:
Resolve a repo + issue (or PR) number to its project_items.id without scanning
the board, mirroring the matching done at webhook ingestion. No GitHub round-trip.
Returns { found: true, item: { id, repo, issue_number, pr_number, title, status } }
when the issue/PR is on the board, or { found: false } when it is not — the latter
is a normal result (webhook lag or an off-board issue), not an error.

issue_number.description: The GitHub issue or PR number to resolve.

name: get_item
title: Get Item Tool
description:
Fetch full details of a single project item by its ID, including
project_fields (the ProjectV2 field catalog with single-select option ids, sourced
live from GitHub) and field_changes (the meta audit trail). Miss Wormwood reads
project_fields to size WSJF Fibonacci values and resolve option ids for update_fields.

blockers.description:
When true, include blocker state (blocked_by + has_open_blockers) via a live
GraphQL pull. Off by default to avoid the extra round-trip.

name: list_development_items
title: List Development Items Tool
description:
Pick the next issue for Dr. Watson to work on: status IN ('In Progress', 'Ready'), issues
only (no PRs), with In Progress first (crash-recovery resume) then Ready, each group ordered
by the GitHub Projects Priority custom field (highest first), excluding items whose
blockedBy dependencies contain any open Issue, and excluding items whose linked open pull
request was opened by someone other than Watson (a human's open PR would otherwise park its
issue at the head of the lane for the life of that PR). Items whose open PR is Watson's own
are still returned — that is the crash-recovery resume path. Also excludes items with an
in-flight claim (see 'claim_item'), so a run already underway is never handed to a second
agent; pass include_claimed=true to see them, which is how Dispatch finds a claim whose run
died and releases it. Live-pulls GraphQL for priority, blockers, and linked-PR provenance on
each candidate. Use limit=1 to get just the top pick.

include_claimed.description:
Include items carrying an in-flight claim (default false). Only Dispatch needs
this — it sweeps claims whose owning run died and releases them. A normal
next-up pick must leave it unset.

limit.description:
Max items to return after priority sort, blocker filter, and foreign-open-PR
filter (1-25, default 1).

name: list_items
title: List Items Tool
description:
Generic debug listing of project items. Accepts optional status, labels, and limit filters.
Use when you need a flexible view not covered by the specialized list_* tools.

labels.description: Comma-separated label filter. Returns items tagged with ANY of the given labels.

status.description:
Status filter. Accepts a single status name ('Ready'), comma-separated list
('Ready,Triage'), or 'null' for items with no status. Omit to include all.

name: list_review_items
title: List Review Items Tool
description:
List project items currently in 'In Review' status — the queue Tracer Bullet
polls to review open PRs. Returns oldest first.

name: list_unrefined_items
title: List Unrefined Items Tool
description:
List project items in the Inbox lane awaiting triage. Miss Wormwood polls this to
pick up new tickets and populate acceptance criteria + WSJF fields. Returns oldest first.

name: move
title: Move Tool
description:
Move a project item to a different Status column (e.g. 'In Progress', 'In Review',
'Done'). Looks up the Status single-select field on the GitHub project, finds the
option matching 'column' by name (case-insensitive), and dispatches
updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue. Declare the acting 'agent' — the move is performed by
that agent's GitHub App. Requires index.mcp.write scope.

agent.description:
The agent identity performing this action: 'holmes', 'watson', or 'lestrade'.
Declare your own name — the action is signed by that agent's GitHub App.

column.description:
Target Status column name (e.g. 'In Progress', 'In Review', 'Done').
Matched case-insensitively against the project's Status options.

id.description: project_items.id of the item to move.

name: release_item
title: Release Item Tool
description:
Clear a project item's in-flight claim so 'list_development_items' offers it again.
Dr. Watson calls this on EVERY exit path — success, budget wind-down, hands-off,
drift, wrong-lane, blocked — and Dispatch calls it to release a claim whose run
died without cleaning up. Idempotent: releasing an unclaimed item succeeds and
reports 'was_claimed' false, so cleanup never becomes an error path. Requires the
index.mcp.write scope.

id.description: The project_items.id to release (NOT the GitHub issue number).

name: set_acceptance_criteria
title: Set Acceptance Criteria Tool
description:
Set an item's acceptance criteria. The AC is maintained as a single dedicated follow-up
comment on the GitHub issue (marked with an HTML comment on its first line) — never the
issue description. Pass the AC as markdown (a checklist) in 'criteria'; the server
find-or-updates that one marked comment, so re-running replaces its content rather than
stacking duplicates. The issue body is never read or written. Inspector Lestrade calls
this instead of editing the issue with gh. Declare the acting 'agent' — the comment is
managed by that agent's GitHub App. Requires index.mcp.write scope.

agent.description:
The agent identity performing this action: 'holmes', 'watson', or 'lestrade'.
Declare your own name — the action is signed by that agent's GitHub App.

criteria.description:
Acceptance criteria as markdown (a `- [ ]` checklist). Do NOT include the
"## Acceptance Criteria" heading — the server adds it. The AC is maintained as
a dedicated marked follow-up comment on the issue, never the issue body.

name: submit_review
title: Submit Review Tool
description:
Submit a pull-request review for a project item — approve or request changes. Sherlock
Holmes calls this instead of `gh pr review`. Pass the acting 'agent', the item id, the
PR number (read via gh), the decision ('approve' or 'request_changes'), and the review
body markdown. The review is posted by the declared agent's GitHub App. Requires
index.mcp.write scope.

agent.description:
The agent identity performing this action: 'holmes', 'watson', or 'lestrade'.
Declare your own name — the action is signed by that agent's GitHub App.

name: update_fields
title: Update Fields Tool
description:
Update one or more ProjectV2 custom fields on an item. 'fields' is a map of
field-name => value. Numeric fields accept numbers, single-select fields accept
the option name (matched case-insensitively). Unsupported field types (iteration,
date) are reported as errors. On org-repo issues this also fans out two GitHub-native
issue attributes the board can't hold: writing 'Priority' derives the issue-level
Priority single-select from the WSJF, and a 'Type' key (or the auto-'PBI' default)
sets the native issue Type — both best-effort, reported under 'issue_writes', and
never fatal to the board write. Declare the acting 'agent' — updates are performed by
that agent's GitHub App (Inspector Lestrade for WSJF scoring during triage). Requires
index.mcp.write scope.

agent.description:
The agent identity performing this action: 'holmes', 'watson', or 'lestrade'.
Declare your own name — the action is signed by that agent's GitHub App.

fields.description:
Map of field name (case-insensitive) to new value. NUMBER fields accept
numeric values; SINGLE_SELECT fields accept the option name; TEXT fields
accept strings. On org-repo issues, writing the 'Priority' NUMBER also
derives the GitHub-native issue Priority single-select (Urgent/High/
Medium/Low) from the WSJF — never pass that as input. A 'Type' key sets
the native issue Type (e.g. 'PBI'); omit it to auto-stamp 'PBI' only when
the issue has no type yet. Both issue-side writes are best-effort and
never fail the board write.
